title: Restriction compatibility for completed rational evaluation
statement: Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and a scheme $X$ on which $\ell$ is invertible. Use the small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], its completed integral coefficient sheaf $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,X}$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients], and the integral operations of [def-pur-integral-derived-operations]. For an object $U$ of this site let $j_U^*$ denote restriction to its slice [def-pur-localized-ringed-site], and form the operations on the slice by the same construction with the restricted coefficient sheaves $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,X}|_U$ and $(A_{E,n})_X|_U$. For $K,M\in D^b_c(X,\mathcal O_E)$ [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed], restriction commutes with derived reduction modulo $\varpi_E^n$, and $j_U^*K,j_U^*M$ are derived complete on the slice, i.e. satisfy the condition of [def-weil-derived-complete] for the reduction towers formed with the restricted coefficient sheaves. Restriction commutes with completed derived tensor and derived internal Hom: there are natural comparison isomorphisms $j_U^*(K\widehat\otimes^L M)\cong j_U^*K\widehat\otimes^L j_U^*M$ and $j_U^*R\mathcal Hom(K,M)\cong R\mathcal Hom(j_U^*K,j_U^*M)$. The first comparison identifies the shifted cones of $1-s$ on the countable products of reductions in the completed tensor construction. These comparisons preserve the coefficient unit and identify restriction of the evaluation comparison $R\mathcal Hom(K,\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,X})\widehat\otimes^L M\to R\mathcal Hom(K,M)$ with the evaluation comparison for $j_U^*K,j_U^*M$, compatibly with successive restriction along $V\to U$. Consequently, after passing to the scalar localizations at $\varpi_E$ [def-weil-linear-scalar-localization] of the $\mathcal O_E$-linear derived categories of module sheaves on $X_{\mathrm{proet}}$ and on the slice, restriction carries the image of the evaluation comparison for $K,M$ to the image of the evaluation comparison for $j_U^*K,j_U^*M$.

source.place: Proof: the termwise identification is compatible with differentials; unit proof: exact functors preserving direct summands. Makes precise restriction of the coefficient dual, completed tensor, and their evaluation before the local bounded-complex argument.

proof.text: Put $B=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,X}$, $B_n=(A_{E,n})_X$, $r=j_U^*$, and choose a containing module universe in which the site and its slices are small. Restriction is exact and has the exact left adjoint $j_{U!}$ by [lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact]. Their termwise functors compute their derived functors, so [lem-pc-derived-adjoint-functors] gives the derived adjunction $j_{U!}\dashv r$. In particular $r$ preserves derived products: for any $T$ on the slice, $\operatorname{Hom}(T,r\prod_i^D Z_i)=\operatorname{Hom}(j_{U!}T,\prod_i^D Z_i)=\prod_i\operatorname{Hom}(T,rZ_i)$. The comparison is the one with components the restricted projections. On sheaves, limits are sectionwise by [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-limits-sectionwise], hence restriction literally commutes with their products and with restriction of scalars along $B\to B_n$. The slice ring is $rB$, with its original coefficient actions, by [def-pur-localized-ringed-site].

source.place: Tag 03DJ (sites-modules-lemma-extension-by-zero-exact); with literature/stacks-project/derived.tex Tag 09T5 (derived-lemma-derived-adjoint-functors); product comparison by the displayed adjunction calculation

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] to the localization morphism of topoi, whose ring map is the identity of $rB$. Module pullback is $B|_U\otimes_{B|_U}(-|_U)$ and is identified with $r$. Thus a flat-term K-flat representative $P$ remains flat-term K-flat after restriction, and the canonical tensor comparison gives $r(P\otimes_B B_n)=rP\otimes_{rB}rB_n$. This computes $r(K\otimes_B^L B_n)\cong rK\otimes_{rB}^L rB_n$, including the quotient transitions and maps from $K$, because all these maps on representatives are induced by the same coefficient projections. This applies to any input complex, including $M$.

For $K$ in the stated category, [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed] supplies a Roos triangle witnessing [def-weil-derived-complete]. Apply the exact derived restriction of step 1 to that triangle. The product comparison of step 1 and the reduction comparison of step 2 carry its first map to the family of reduction maps for $rK$ and its middle map to $1-s_U$: component $n$ is projection to $n$ minus transition composed with projection to $n+1$. The resulting distinguished triangle is exactly the derived-completeness condition on the slice. Repeat with $M$. No assertion about constructibility on the slice or a new uniform amplitude bound is needed for this conclusion.

proof.text: Choose flat-term K-flat representatives $P,Q$ of any two inputs. The integral tensor of [def-pur-integral-derived-operations] is the specified shifted cone for the strict tower $C_n=\operatorname{Res}_n\operatorname{Tot}(P_n\otimes_{B_n}Q_n)$. By [lem-weil-proetale-countable-products-exact] and [lem-weil-derived-limit-existence], the ambient termwise products represent derived products. Step 2 identifies $rC_n$ with the slice tower used in the same construction. Step 1 therefore identifies its termwise product with the product in the slice derived category as well. Exact restriction commutes with finite direct sums, shifts and the explicit mapping-cone differential. Consequently it carries $\operatorname{Cone}(1-s)[-1]$ to $\operatorname{Cone}(1-s_U)[-1]$, yielding the asserted completed tensor comparison. It also preserves the canonical map from the ordinary tensor to this cone: on a representative it is $z\mapsto((z\bmod\varpi_E^n)_n,0)$. This is a comparison of actual complexes, not a uniqueness assertion for arbitrary triangulated cones. Functoriality under changing representatives is [lem-pur-integral-operations-well-defined].

source.place: Tags 08TC, 0941; Bhatt–Scholze Definition 3.4.10; explicit cone comparison

proof.text: The internal Hom in the item is ordinary ringed-site derived internal Hom, by [def-pur-integral-derived-operations]. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-internal-hom-exact-restriction] supplies $rH(L,N)\cong H_U(rL,rN)$ for all unbounded inputs, where $H=R\mathcal Hom_B$. Use its model normalization from [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-slice-evaluation-transpose]: restrict a K-injective representative of the second variable and identify the local families of module maps. This gives precisely the asserted comparison for $K,M$ and also for $K,B$. The coefficient object restricts to $rB[0]$ with the identity coefficient action. All the comparisons so far compose under $V\to U$, since further slice restriction just forgets one more structural arrow and the maps of sections, quotient towers, products and cone coordinates are unchanged.

We now identify the completion unit used to define completed evaluation. By [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-integers-dvr], $\mathcal O_E$ is a PID contained in $E$ and $\varpi_E\ne0$; all its ideals are therefore finitely generated, so it is Noetherian. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-completed-constant-sheaf-reduction] with $A=\mathcal O_E$ and $I=(\varpi_E)$. The free resolution $[A\xrightarrow{\varpi_E^n}A]$ of $A/\varpi_E^n$, in degrees $[-1,0]$, gives a quasi-isomorphism $Q_n=[B\xrightarrow{\varpi_E^n}B]\to B_n$. The transition on $Q_n$ is $(\varpi_E,1)$; the quotient maps therefore give a strict map of towers. The same assertion holds after exact restriction to any slice. For a flat-term K-flat representative $P$ of $Z$, tensoring these maps with $P$ gives a levelwise quasi-isomorphism to its reduction tower. Taking total derived inverse limits preserves this quasi-isomorphism, by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit]. By [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-cech-koszul-dual-limit] its source is canonically $H(C_{\varpi_E},Z)$, where $C_{\varpi_E}=[B\to B[1/\varpi_E]]$. The unit is the strict-tower unit, not an arbitrary lift of the projections. By [lem-weil-pbc-extended-cech-completion-model], this identifies $C(Z)=R\lim_n\operatorname{Res}_n(Z\otimes_B^L B_n)$, with this unit $\eta_Z$, as the reflection into locally derived $(\varpi_E)$-complete objects. These statements apply on every slice with $rB,rB_n$ too.

proof.text:
The completeness condition of the item implies the local completeness in step 6. Indeed the Roos triangle in [def-weil-derived-complete] identifies its object, with its maps to the reductions, with their total derived limit; this total limit is $C(Z)$ of step 6 and is locally complete. Local completeness is invariant under isomorphism. Hence $M$ and $rM$ are locally complete by step 3. Moreover $H(K,M)$ is locally complete: for every further slice $W$ and every $f\in(\varpi_E)B(W)$, the internal-Hom and restriction calculus of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-internal-hom-exact-restriction] gives
$$H_W(B_W[1/f],H_W(K_W,M_W))\cong H_W(K_W,H_W(B_W[1/f],M_W))=0.$$
The exchange uses the two tensor-Hom currying isomorphisms and tensor symmetry; the last equality is exactly local completeness of $M$. The same computation gives local completeness of $H_U(rK,rM)$. In particular precomposition with $\eta_Z$ induces a bijection $\operatorname{Hom}(C(Z),H(K,M))\cong\operatorname{Hom}(Z,H(K,M))$, and likewise on the slice, by the reflection in step 6.

Set $D_K=H(K,B)$ and $Z=D_K\otimes_B^L M$. Let $u:Z\to H(K,M)$ be the ordinary evaluation comparison: its tensor-Hom adjunct is
$$(D_K\otimes^L M)\otimes^L K\longrightarrow(D_K\otimes^L K)\otimes^L M\xrightarrow{\operatorname{ev}_{K,B}\otimes1}B\otimes^L M\longrightarrow M.$$
The first arrow is tensor associativity and the symmetry interchanging $M,K$; the last is the coefficient unitor. [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-slice-evaluation-transpose] says that the canonical restriction comparisons preserve the counit, transposition and Koszul symmetry. The tensor comparison is the termwise one of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback]; on pure tensors it preserves reassociation and $b\otimes m\mapsto bm$. Thus the displayed adjunct restricts to the identical displayed adjunct on the slice, and transposition shows that $r(u)$ is the ordinary slice comparison under step 5.

source.place: Tags 08J9, 08JB and 07A4; explicit adjunct and coefficient-unit normalization

proof.text:
There is a canonical identification $C(Z)=D_K\widehat\otimes^L M$: using K-flat representatives $P,Q$, its level-$n$ identification is the balanced tensor isomorphism
$$(P\otimes_B Q)\otimes_B B_n\cong(P\otimes_B B_n)\otimes_{B_n}(Q\otimes_B B_n),\quad(p\otimes q)\otimes a\mapsto(p\otimes1)\otimes(q\otimes a).$$
Its inverse multiplies the two $B_n$-coefficients, and these formulas commute with differentials, quotient transitions, and the unit maps. The completed evaluation comparison is the adjunct of evaluation under the completed tensor-Hom adjunction (Bhatt–Scholze Lemma 3.4.11), whose transposition is precomposition with the completion unit; thus it is the unique arrow $\widehat u:C(Z)\to H(K,M)$ with $\widehat u\eta_Z=u$, using step 7. The product/cone comparison of step 4 also identifies $rC(Z)$ with $C_U(rZ)$ and $r\eta_Z$ with $\eta_{rZ}$. Restrict the equality $\widehat u\eta_Z=u$ and use step 8. Both the transported $r\widehat u$ and the slice completed evaluation now extend the same ordinary comparison along $\eta_{rZ}$ into the locally complete target $H_U(rK,rM)$. The bijection in step 7 makes them equal. This proves compatibility of the actual completed evaluation morphisms, and the same uniqueness proves its coherence under successive restriction. For a complete input $L$, the coefficient-unit constraint is $C(L\otimes_B^L B)\cong C(L)\xrightarrow{\eta_L^{-1}}L$; step 7 and the reflector make $\eta_L$ invertible. Since restriction preserves both $\eta_L$ and the ordinary unitor, the completed comparisons preserve this coefficient-unit constraint too.

source.place: Tag 099F universal property; Bhatt–Scholze Definition 3.4.10 and Lemma 3.4.11; balanced tensor formula written explicitly

proof.text: Restriction is $\mathcal O_E$-linear because its action on module morphisms is sectionwise. It therefore induces the functor between the scalar localizations [def-weil-linear-scalar-localization], given on morphisms by $f\otimes a\mapsto r(f)\otimes a$. This respects identities and composition by $r(gf)=r(g)r(f)$ and the displayed bilinear composition law in that definition. Applying it to the equality of completed evaluation maps in step 9 gives the stated equality of their images after inverting $\varpi_E$. Applying it to the identity and composition equalities of the comparisons also preserves their coherence. This argument only uses scalar localization of Hom modules and makes no identification with a different coefficient category.
